newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer but remains vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer but remains vulnerable.

text.p: Precious metals prices were steady to firmer on Monday encouraging dealers to forecast further strength for most of them.
They were less sanguine about gold, albeit that it fixed at $341.00 per ounce against $339.75 on Friday afternoon, its lowest fixing since April 22, 1993.
"There is nothing to say this market is going all the way back up just now," one dealer said.
An advance to $343-$344 might be possible but "nothing much has changed, the market is still bearish", he added.
One thing which had changed, he said, was more attention was being paid to the the U.S. dollar whose soaring strength had put pressure on gold all year.
"The dollar may be helping today. It is being watched and it is some time since we had an outside factor in this market," the dealer said.

The attention on the dollar followed a communique after the Berlin summit meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) industrial counties that said they believed the "misalignments in exchange markets...have been corrected" and that they favoured stability in the currency markets.
The correction was seen referring to the dollar and the yen which had adjusted from weakness and strength resepctively.
Technical analayst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge noted that gold was now more oversold than it had been for 10 years.
"Whilst it is difficult to argue there is any sign of a recovery there certainly is good excuse for support in this region to hold for now," she said.
Dealers were less sure about specifying a floor for the market. "There is too much emotion about to be able to point to a particular number on the charts," one said.
Silver edged a couple of cents off its firm close on Friday when a 16-cent range reflected a bout of buying and short covering late in the day.
"That was an amazing about turn on Friday and silver could be about to re-establish itself," a dealer said.
It was indicated at $4.92/$4.93 down a cent at midday.
Palladium fixed at a fresh recent high of $133.75, its top fixing since July 22, 1996 as consumners continued to cover in the dealer market against delayed Russian expoprts.
Speculator buying was also cited as being behind the firm price which was up $3.25 at $133.50/$134.50.
Sister metal platinum was $2.25 firmer at $351.25/$352.25 taking strength both from palladium and its widening premium over gold, dealers said.
